2607.02464.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
2607.02464.paper_summary: Large Language Model (LLM) social simulations are a promising research method, but they are not yet faithful enough to be adopted widely. In this work, we investigate whether the current scaling paradigm in language modeling is likely to close these gaps, or whether simulation fidelity is orthogonal to general capabilities and therefore deserving of more research attention. We use scaling laws to study the relationship between LLMs' compute scale, general capability benchmarks, and the fidelity of social simulation in three representative sub-domains: opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, and longitudinal forecasting. Surprisingly, we discover strong compute scaling in all three settings, using a suite of 85 transformer LLMs with the Qwen3 architecture pre-trained on the DCLM web text corpus under fixed-compute budgets from $10^{18}$ to $10^{20}$ FLOPs. Then we evaluate 35 larger and more capable open-weight models up to 70B parameters, allowing us to predict downstream accuracy from loss. This reveals that the majority of behavioral and opinion simulation tasks will rapidly improve with scale, particularly when they involve populations that are well-represented in English web corpora. Longitudinal forecasting and underrepresented opinions scale more slowly, especially when they are less correlated with general knowledge and reasoning benchmarks like MMLU. In behavior simulation, scaling fails to improve model calibration with human cognitive biases like risk aversion, as well as human heuristics like learning correlated rewards from related tasks. On these tasks, even fine-tuned models fail to noticeably scale up performance from 0.5B to 8B parameters. Taken together, we conclude that scale will improve social simulations in most settings, but outliers exist, and improvements will be less reliable in low-resource domains.
2607.02464.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）社會模擬是一種有前景的研究方法，但尚未足夠忠實以被廣泛採用。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們探討當前語言建模中的擴展範式是否能夠彌補這些差距，或者模擬的真實性是否與一般能力正交，因此值得更多的研究關注。<lb/>我們使用擴展法則來研究LLM的計算規模、一般能力基準和社會模擬的真實性之間的關係，涵蓋三個代表性的子領域：意見建模、行為模擬和長期預測。<lb/>令人驚訝的是，我們在這三個設定中發現強大的計算擴展，使用了一組85個基於Qwen3架構的TransformerLLM，這些模型在固定計算預算下的DCLM網絡文本語料庫上進行了預訓練，計算範圍從$10^{18}$到$10^{20}$ FLOPs。<lb/>然後，我們評估了35個更大且更具能力的開放權重模型，參數數量高達70B，這使我們能夠從損失預測下游準確性。<lb/>這顯示出大多數行為和意見模擬任務會隨著規模的增長而迅速改善，特別是當它們涉及在英語網絡語料庫中得到良好代表的人群時。<lb/>長期預測和少數意見的擴展速度較慢，特別是當它們與一般知識和推理基準（如MMLU）相關性較低時。<lb/>在行為模擬中，擴展未能改善模型對人類認知偏見（如風險厭惡）以及人類啟發式（如從相關任務中學習相關獎勵）的校準。<lb/>在這些任務中，即使是微調過的模型也未能顯著提高從0.5B到8B參數的性能。<lb/>綜合來看，我們得出結論，規模將在大多數情境中改善社會模擬，但存在異常情況，並且在資源匱乏的領域中，改進的可靠性會降低。
